analysis.title: Tenaris (TENR.MI): Strong 3Q beat; 4Q step-up sets a higher baseline into 2027
key_insights: Tenaris 3Q26 EBITDA was $756mn, 17% above Visible Alpha consensus of $647mn. Net income attributable to shareholders was $509mn, 21% above consensus of $420mn.
Tubes sales volumes were 976kt, 3% above consensus of 948kt. Tubes EBITDA was $775/t, 13% above consensus of $683/t. In 2Q26 volumes were 947kt and EBITDA/t was $686/t.

The qoq improvement came from higher volumes on higher demand in North America, more shipments to Middle East customers, favourable product mix, better fixed-cost absorption and lower maintenance expenses. Higher raw material, logistics and energy costs partly offset it.

Management reported increased Middle East shipments in 3Q, including deliveries to Kuwait and Iraq. Regional drilling activity has slowly started to recover, although disruption through the Strait of Hormuz (SoH) continues.

3Q cash flow from operations was $636mn pre-working capital. After $98mn capex, FCF pre-working capital was $538mn. Reported FCF after a $270mn working-capital build was $268mn. Net cash was $3.8bn versus $3.6bn at the end of 2Q26.

Management expects a further increase in sales and EBITDA in 4Q26 on higher OCTG demand and prices in North America and more shipments to offshore projects. It expects 4Q to set a new quarterly baseline for sales and EBITDA going into 2027, assuming no significant change in the geopolitical context.
GS says 3Q results and guidance imply at least 4% upside to FY26 consensus EBITDA of $2,790mn. With 9M26 EBITDA at $2,141mn and 4Q guided above $756mn, FY26 EBITDA would be above $2,897mn.

FY27 consensus EBITDA of $3,285mn implies average quarterly EBITDA of $821mn, about 9% above the 3Q26 level. GS says FY27 consensus looks increasingly well underpinned but it would need more visibility on 4Q EBITDA and 2027 volume and pricing to argue for meaningful upside.
GS expects a positive share-price reaction to the results, potentially mid-single digit.
GS stays Neutral with a 12-month price target of €28.7 for TENR.MI and $65.0 for the TS ADR, using 8x EV/EBITDA and a 7% FCF yield weighted 50/50.

market_movers.rationale: GS stays Neutral after a 3Q beat and guidance for a higher 4Q baseline. It sees at least 4% upside to FY26 consensus EBITDA but not yet material upside for 2027. ADR price was $55.92 on 4 Nov, implying 16.2% upside to target.

sector_views.rationale: North America OCTG demand and prices are rising, Middle East shipments are recovering and offshore project shipments are increasing. GS wants more visibility on 2027 volume and pricing before arguing for upside.

earnings_insights: Tenaris 3Q26 reported EBITDA $756mn vs Visible Alpha consensus $647mn (GS estimate $643mn), 17% above consensus. Reported 11/4-11/5 (3Q26 actual).
Tenaris 3Q26 reported net income attributable to shareholders $509mn vs consensus $420mn (GS estimate $390mn), 21% above consensus.
Tenaris 3Q26 reported EPS $0.50 vs consensus $0.42 (GS estimate $0.39), 20% above consensus. 3Q25 EPS was $0.43 and 2Q26 EPS was $0.47.
Tenaris 3Q26 reported revenue $3,102mn vs consensus $2,996mn, 4% above consensus, up 4% yoy and 5% qoq. EBITDA margin was 24% vs 22% in 2Q26.
3Q26 tax rate was 21% vs GS estimate of 25% and 14% in 2Q26.

4Q26 guidance: further sequential rise in sales and EBITDA above the 3Q26 reported $756mn. This compares with prior 2Q26 guidance that 2H sales and EBITDA would stay broadly in line with 1H26 EBITDA of $1,385mn.
GS FY26E consensus EBITDA is $2,790mn and FY27 consensus EBITDA is $3,285mn. GS FY26E EPS is $1.87 and FY27E EPS is $2.20.
GS asks on the call how much of the previously delayed c.$130mn of Middle East revenues was recognized in 3Q and how much is expected in 4Q26 versus 2027.
risk_factors: Higher or lower oil prices and drilling activity than currently anticipated.
Higher or lower US tariff rates or changes in trade policy.
Higher or lower cash returns to shareholders.
Higher or lower capex and value-dilutive or accretive investments, including M&A.
Continued disruption through the Strait of Hormuz affecting Middle East shipments.
geopolitical: Disruption through the Strait of Hormuz continues while Middle East drilling activity has slowly started to recover. Tenaris shipped to Kuwait and Iraq in 3Q.
Management's 4Q baseline guidance assumes no significant change in the geopolitical context.
